title: Hattin: The Day Thirst Surrendered Jerusalem
summary: Recounts how, on the fourth of July, eleven eighty-seven, at the Horns of Hattin in Galilee, Saladin drew the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem under King Guy de Lusignan into a waterless march and destroyed it, and covers the capture of the True Cross and the execution of Raynald de Châtillon. The episode ranges from the night council that decided to leave the springs of Sephoria to the siege of Tiberias, from the iced sherbet offered in the tent at Hattin to the surrender of Jerusalem without bloodshed in October eleven eighty-seven, and on to the Third Crusade.
